surface: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and Audience Network placements bought in Ads Manager
configurable_click: 1-day or 7-day after a link click, set at ad-set level
configurable_view: 1 day after an impression. A third setting, engage-through, counts 1 day after a non-link click, and the page warns that some accounts still run the previous versions of click-through and engage-through while the change rolls out
timestamp_basis: verify-in-account. Selectable; the Marketing API reference, updated 27 July 2026, exposes action_report_time with impression, conversion, mixed and lifetime and gives the worked case - seen on the first, converted on the second, reported on the first under impression - while no interface default is published on either page
view_through_in_default_number: yes. When the ad set uses a view window, view-through conversions sit inside the Results column
where_to_read_it: Ads Manager > ad set level for the setting, which the help page says is where both the model and the windows are chosen; Columns > Customise columns > Attribution setting for what a given report is showing
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: The headline number includes conversions from people who never clicked. Analytics has no such concept, so one order is a Meta conversion and an Organic Search session at the same time and both records are correct.

surface: Search, Display, Video, Demand Gen and Performance Max
configurable_click: 1 to 90 days, and the permitted range depends on the conversion source
configurable_view: 1 to 30 days, or 1 to 4 weeks on some surfaces. The engaged-view conversion window defaults to 3 days
timestamp_basis: click date. A conversion is reported against the date of the click rather than the date it happened; columns labelled (by conv. time) opt into the other view
view_through_in_default_number: no. View-through conversions are excluded from the Conversions column and appear only in View-through conversions and All conversions. Engaged-view conversions are the opposite and are included in Conversions
where_to_read_it: Goals > Conversions > Summary > the conversion action > Edit settings. The click-date basis is a property of the report rather than a setting, so it cannot be turned off - only added to
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: A 30-day window against an analytics lookback of 30 or 90 days, reported on a different calendar. A conversion today from a click last Tuesday lands in last week's row here and this week's row in analytics, so a week-over-week comparison built from both tools compares two incompatible calendars.

surface: Website and app streams. The analytics side that every platform number gets compared against
default_click_window: 30 days for acquisition key events, 90 days for every other key event
default_view_window: engaged-view 3 days. There is no view-through conversion
configurable_click: acquisition 30 or 7 days; other key events 90, 60 or 30 days
timestamp_basis: event time, with ad interaction time available as the alternative in reporting
view_through_in_default_number: no. GA4 has no view-through conversion at all, which is most of the gap on view-heavy channels
where_to_read_it: Admin > Attribution settings for the model and the windows. The reporting time basis is chosen per report rather than per property
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: It disagrees with itself first: session-scoped and user-scoped dimensions always use paid-and-organic last click whatever the property's model is set to, so two tables in one tool can differ. Against Google Ads, only key events where Google Ads is the last non-direct click become conversions there, and the two products run on different time zones.

platform: TikTok Ads Manager, campaigns without a connected shop
surface: In-feed placements bought in Ads Manager that do not sell through a TikTok Shop
default_click_window: verify-in-account. Three live help pages list what can be selected and none of them names a default
default_view_window: verify-in-account. Same three pages, same silence on the default
configurable_click: 1, 7, 14 or 28 days on the two ad-group pages, last updated November 2025 and July 2026. A third page still live and last updated February 2025 says 1 or 7 only, scoped to accounts moved onto TikTok's Self-Attributing Network and nowhere labelled superseded. The vendor contradicts itself in public, so read the account rather than the documentation
configurable_view: Off, 1 or 7 days on the two newer pages; Off or 1 day on the February 2025 page. Engaged view-through is a separate setting offering 1 or 7 days
timestamp_basis: impression time for view-through purchases, per the metrics glossary. The click-through basis is verify-in-account
where_to_read_it: Ads Manager > ad group > Bidding and optimisation > Attribution settings, and read it before publishing rather than after, because the page is explicit that attribution settings cannot be changed once the ad group is published - a different window needs a new ad group. That makes this the one row in this table where getting it wrong is not correctable in the account
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: Nobody can state the gap until the window is read out of the account, because the vendor publishes two different sets of selectable windows on pages that are both live. Whatever it turns out to be, it is frozen at publish time, so a media plan that assumed 7-day click on an ad group set to 28 is comparing two different measurements and cannot fix it retrospectively.

surface: Product Shopping Ads and GMV Max campaigns selling through a connected TikTok Shop
configurable_click: 7 days, plus a 30-minute click window on LIVE Shopping Ads that applies only to orders placed inside the liveroom, chosen in Bidding and optimisation
timestamp_basis: day of touch. The order is recorded against the day of the click or impression, not the day it was placed, so an order seven days after the click lands in the earlier week
view_through_in_default_number: yes, but clicks take precedence over views. The order goes to the most recent interaction and one order is never split across two ads
where_to_read_it: Ads Manager > Bidding and optimisation for the LIVE window; Ads Manager > Attribution Manager for the metric definitions, including a separate Assisted (Shop) family on a 28-day exposure window
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: Attribution is keyed to the Shop ID and explicitly not to the product ID, so an ad for one table can be credited with the order for a different one and the per-product read is not what it looks like. The Assisted (Shop) metrics use a 28-day exposure window with no equivalent in any other tool, so two columns of the same interface are counting different things.

surface: Shop Ads dashboard and Data Compass. The reports a Vietnamese seller actually opens
configurable_click: not set here. The report states the 7-day window in each of its four sections
timestamp_basis: order date, which is the opposite of Ads Manager and the single largest reason the two disagree
where_to_read_it: Seller Center > Analytics > Sales performance > Breakdown for the revenue split; Shop Ads > Ads Dashboard and Data Compass > Overview for the ads-versus-affiliate split
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: Three reasons and the vendor publishes a page for them. It buckets by the day the order was placed while Ads Manager buckets by the day of the click, so one order sits in two different weeks. It sees every ad account running for the shop while Ads Manager sees one. And in Vietnam specifically the report shows only Product Shopping Ads created in Seller Center on the primary ad account and excludes everything built in Ads Manager, so the two totals are not describing the same campaigns at all.

surface: Off-platform traffic tracking (Traffic Ngoại sàn) for anything you drive into a Shopee listing, and the in-app Video display service (Dịch vụ hiển thị Video)
default_click_window: 7 days on the video display service, stated inside the metric definitions rather than offered as a setting. The UTM traffic report has no window at all, because it splits visits, orders and revenue by channel instead of attributing across a lookback
default_view_window: none published. Views are a reported metric on the video display service, not an attribution path to an order
configurable_click: no. The seven days is part of what the two metrics mean
timestamp_basis: verify-in-account. Neither the video display metrics page nor the off-platform traffic page says whether an order is dated by the click or by the order
view_through_in_default_number: no. Both metrics require a click on the product in the video
where_to_read_it: Phân tích bán hàng > Truy cập > Traffic Ngoại sàn for the UTM builder, the link manager and the channel report; Shopee app > Shopee Video > Dịch vụ hiển thị > Báo cáo Dịch vụ hiển thị Video for the seven-day metrics. Build the link under 250 characters or the deep link is unsupported and you fall back to web
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: Two rules inside one product, which is the part people miss. Số đơn hàng counts every order placed within seven days of a click on the product in the video; Doanh thu counts revenue only where that click was the last one to the product in the same seven days. So the order count and the money are not measuring the same thing and their ratio is not an average order value. Separately the off-platform traffic report runs two days behind, and Shopee's own page says that may leave it inconsistent with what other channels report - a vendor stating the asymmetry in advance for once. The seller affiliate programme is a separate document and it publishes two windows that contradict each other: definition 1.2 retains visit information for 7 days while definition 1.4 counts an order completed within 30 days of the visitor arriving, and the terms never reconcile them. Model both and confirm the operative one with your Shopee contact before a forecast depends on it - see data/affiliate-mechanics.csv and affiliate-commerce.md.

surface: Open Platform order endpoints. The only Lazada surface carrying order data that can be read without a seller login, which is why it is the only one this row can speak for
default_click_window: verify-in-account. No page reachable without a seller login publishes one
where_to_read_it: path-unpublished. Lazada documents neither the window nor the screen it sits on, so this row will not invent a menu path. The API documentation handler at open.lazada.com answers without a login and exposes no analytics or attribution endpoint, and the category tree is drawn by the browser rather than served, so even the list of what exists needs an account. Ask a seller with access to open the ads interface, read the window out of it, and send back a screenshot of the screen it came from - that screenshot is the citation this row cannot have on its own.
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: The order record has no channel in it to disagree with. `/order/get` publishes 49 distinct output field names and `/orders/get` publishes 55, both last modified 2022-07-25, and neither carries a source, referrer, channel, campaign, affiliate or sub-identifier field. So spend driven into a Lazada listing is measurable on your own side up to the click, and after that only as a before-and-after read on Lazada's own totals. Write that into the plan before the spend rather than into the report afterwards. The row exists to record the absence, because a platform missing from this table is a platform somebody will assume runs on Meta's 7-day default.

surface: Website, Video and Display ads measured by the Zalo Ads pixel, plus the Chat Now and Call buttons that land a user in an Official Account
default_click_window: verify-in-account. No click window is published anywhere on Zalo's help centre or developer documentation. Two 7-day figures on the site are not windows and get quoted as though they were: a conversion is tagged Đang hoạt động when it has recorded at least one event in the last 7 days, and a separate article argues for scheduling an ad across 7 days
default_view_window: verify-in-account. No view-through conversion is documented at all
configurable_click: nothing configurable is published. The only conversion-side choices are which pixel supplies the data - Pixel của tôi against the LadiPage universal pixel, which the conversion library does not support - and which saved conversion the ad optimises toward, of which only Trở thành khách hàng tiềm năng, Hoàn tất mua hàng and Liên hệ are eligible
timestamp_basis: verify-in-account. The report glossary defines eight metrics - Lượt hiển thị, Lượt nhấn, CTR, Lượt liên hệ, Giá trung bình, Chi phí, Số người xem, Tần số - and none of them is an attribution metric
view_through_in_default_number: there is no view-through metric to include. Something else inflates the headline instead: Tổng conversion is ad conversions plus organic conversions plus conversions driven by other advertisers' ads, so Zalo's total is deliberately not ad-attributed
where_to_read_it: Ad account > Thư viện > Conversion for the pixel code, the saved conversions and their reports; then the ad's Chọn nguồn dữ liệu field to pick Pixel của tôi and one saved conversion. There is no attribution-window screen to open, which is why the window columns name no default rather than a menu. Whether an ad that opens an OA chat can be traced to that ad is also verify-in-account: the ads report counts Lượt liên hệ in aggregate, and this row does not claim what the OA webhooks carry because those pages serve no readable text without a browser
why_it_disagrees_with_analytics: Zalo appends its own click identifier `zaclid` to the landing-page URL, and publishes the steps for stripping it out of Google Analytics - Exclude URL Query Parameters in GA3, a Trim Query variable on Page URL feeding page_location in GA4. That instruction is the useful half, because a platform telling you to remove its parameter is a platform confirming the query string survives the click, so your own UTM tagging is what identifies Zalo traffic on your side. The disagreeing half is Tổng conversion, which adds organic conversions and other advertisers' conversions to yours and is therefore comparable to no analytics number at all - read Conversion từ QC instead. Events are also defined differently here: a conversion fires on a URL keyword or on a button's ID, class or text rather than on a tracking call, so a redesign that renames a button silently stops the conversion without breaking any code.
